channel.title: Institute of Welsh Affairs - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Institute of Welsh Affairs (iwa.wales)

item.title: How can the next Welsh Government deliver local economic growth and development through a just transition that benefits future generations? - Institute of Welsh Affairs
item.description: Wales Centre for Public Policy’s Dr Helen Tilley expands on the first webinar delivered in partnership with the IWA

item.title: Wales’ Hearts Need More: BHF Cymru’s call to action - Institute of Welsh Affairs
item.description: British Heart Foundation (BHF) Cymru explain how between 700 and 800 lives in Wales could be saved in 2035 if the next Welsh Government commit to reducing premature deaths from cardiovascular disease.

item.title: LONG READ: New economic governance: An answer, but what’s the question? - Institute of Welsh Affairs
item.description: Joe Rossiter considers Plaid Cymru’s key economic proposal of creating a new Welsh Development Agency

item.title: How will broadcasters report the 2026 Senedd election campaign? - Institute of Welsh Affairs
item.description: Professor Stephen Cushion examines how impartiality and political accountability are important factors for news outlets to consider while covering the Senedd election.

item.title: After the shake-up: Why active travel must remain a priority for the next Welsh Government - Institute of Welsh Affairs
item.description: Tomos Owens discusses why the new Welsh Government must prioritise active travel.

item.title: Bridging the gap: Enhancing advocacy and inclusion for minoritised communities with learning disabilities in Wales - Institute of Welsh Affairs
item.description: Edward Oloidi looks at the ways organisations can be more approachable and inclusive of people with learning disabilities from ethnic minority communities.

item.title: The Welsh Government is cutting funding for Adult Autism & ADHD services - Institute of Welsh Affairs
item.description: Kaja shares their thoughts after receiving a letter during Neurodivergence Celebration Week outlining the Welsh Government’s plan to re-direct funding away from the adult autism and ADHD services.

item.title: When the rules collapse, Cymru must speak for peace and justice as war expands in the Middle East - Institute of Welsh Affairs
item.description: Dr Hade Turkmen from Oxfam Cymru discusses the rising conflicts in the Middle East and calls for Cymru to stand firmly against the expansion of war and the collapse of the rules that protect civilians everywhere.

item.title: Community cohesion and social infrastructure – the vital connections - Institute of Welsh Affairs
item.description: Chris Johnes, CEO of Building Communities Trust, discusses how social infrastructure and local services are integral to community cohesion.

item.title: The next step of the long journey to empowering our communities - Institute of Welsh Affairs
item.description: Joe Rossiter reflects on the final report of the Community Asset Commission’s Task and Finish Group

item.title: Pulling devolved levers to help tackle poverty in Wales - Institute of Welsh Affairs
item.description: Joe Rossiter reflects on the second webinar - Turning the Tide on Child Poverty - delivered in partnership between the IWA and WCPP
